Completely free and built for the common man."

posts.name: VaniQ

posts.description: Every dictation app turns useAuthSession into "use auth session". VaniQ reads the repo you're working in first, so your own identifiers beat the phonetically similar English. Superwhisper and MacWhisper run locally but use general models, so they mangle the same names. Reading your repo is the difference.

posts.name: ClipShrink
posts.tagline: Free, private in-browser video compression using WebAssembly
posts.description: ClipShrink is a free, client-side video compressor that shrinks MP4, MOV, and WebM videos directly in your browser using local WebAssembly. Unlike traditional cloud compressors, files never touch remote servers—ensuring 100% privacy, zero upload queues, and no watermarks. Includes automated presets to fit exact platform upload limits: Discord (8MB), WhatsApp (16MB), Gmail (25MB), Outlook (20MB), and Slack (10MB).

posts.name: Wikly
posts.tagline: 100% Free & local only tiny space to GTD ✅
posts.description: I built Wikly because I got tired of productivity apps that felt like they needed their own productivity system. Wikly is a tiny desk for getting things done. Write down your tasks, start a timer, and focus. No account. No subscriptions. No complicated setup. Your data stays on your device. It’s completely free, forever. I built it mostly for myself, but figured someone else might find it useful too. 😄 If you try it, I’d love to hear what you think, what’s missing, or what you’d change.
